claude_proposed_widenings.name: passive_grant (class feature family)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The feature grants a permanent benefit at level-up with no activation cost, no use_count resource, and no rest reset. The only existing class feature family is 'activation', which requires all three of those. A 'passive_grant' (or 'level_choice') family is needed for features that are permanently acquired rather than activated at runtime.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see 'Feats' for feats). Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: grant_feat
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The primary mechanic is granting a feat (one of the Fighting Style feats). No 'grant_feat' atom exists in v4 taxonomy or the surface types. This is distinct from 'grant_spell_access' — it grants an entire feat, not just spell access.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see 'Feats' for feats).

claude_proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access in ClassFeatureEffect
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Blessed Warrior option grants access to two Cleric cantrips with a specified spellcasting ability (Charisma). The v4 taxonomy has a 'grant_spell_access' effect atom, but ClassFeatureEffect in types.ts only has GrantExtraActionEffect | HealHpEffect. This variant needs to be added to ClassFeatureEffect to encode Blessed Warrior.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You learn two Cleric cantrips of your choice... The chosen cantrips count as Paladin spells for you, and Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: choose_option mechanic (level-up menu)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The feature presents a menu: pick a Fighting Style feat OR pick Blessed Warrior. This is a 'choose one from set' pattern at level-up. No surface shape captures a top-level class feature that branches into mutually exclusive options at character-creation/level-up time.
